claims.text: The target alloy begins as an initially single-phase, homogeneous high-entropy alloy.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi is an example of a compositionally complex high-entropy alloy.
The initial alloy contains coherent nanoscale precipitates.
Prolonged high-temperature exposure promotes localized grain-boundary segregation in an initially single-phase high-entropy alloy.
Grain-boundary segregation triggers nucleation and growth of incoherent, brittle secondary-phase precipitates at grain boundaries.
The grain-boundary precipitates degrade toughness by promoting intergranular fracture.
Brittleness in conventional alloys is predominantly driven by continuous grain-boundary films or coarse intermetallic precipitates.
The compositionally complex HEA matrix initially delays segregation-related precipitation and embrittlement.
A critical level of grain-boundary segregation must be reached before incoherent precipitates form.
Even minute incoherent grain-boundary precipitates can compromise intergranular cohesion.
Incoherent grain-boundary precipitates act as crack-initiation sites leading to brittle failure.
Thermal aging will reduce fracture toughness relative to the unaged baseline.
Thermal aging will increase intergranular cracking and reduce crack-propagation resistance.
Aged specimens will exhibit localized incoherent secondary-phase particles at grain boundaries.
The unaged homogeneous baseline has high toughness and ductility.
Temperatures of 700–900 °C and low strain rates represent the proposed service and loading regime for the mechanism.
The proposed mechanism may not apply under rapid thermal cycling or at very low service temperatures.

contradictions.description: The alloy is repeatedly described as initially single-phase and homogeneous while also being described as containing coherent nanoscale precipitates or features, which ordinarily imply a compositionally or structurally distinct precipitate phase.
